sets.title: Research Tower
sets.contentHtml:
Five researchers, Kavya, Lalit, Meera, Naveen and Omkar, have their labs in a five-storey research tower, one lab on each floor. The floors are numbered 1 (lowest) to 5 (top). The five researchers come from five different cities, Pune, Surat, Kochi, Indore and Ranchi, and specialise in five different fields, Genomics, Robotics, Optics, Polymers and Acoustics.

The following is known:

  1. The researcher from Kochi works on a lower floor than the Robotics specialist.
  2. There is exactly one floor between the floors of Kavya and Lalit.
  3. The researcher on the top floor specialises in Optics, or is from Indore, or both.
  4. Meera is from Pune.
  5. The Polymers specialist and the researcher from Surat work on adjacent floors.
  6. Omkar works on a lower floor than Naveen.
  7. The Genomics specialist is from Surat.
  8. There are at least two floors between the floors of the Acoustics specialist and the Optics specialist.
  9. The researcher from Pune works on the floor immediately above the Acoustics specialist.
  10. Lalit works on the floor immediately above the researcher from Surat.

sets.title: Two-Round Cook-Off
sets.contentHtml:
Six chefs, Ishaan, Jhanvi, Kabir, Lavanya, Manav and Nikita, took part in a two-round cooking contest. In each round the judges ranked all six chefs. Ties were allowed, and ranks followed the standard competition convention: a chef's rank is 1 more than the number of chefs placed strictly ahead of him or her. For example, if two chefs tie for the top place, both get rank 1 and the next chef gets rank 3.

A chef's total is the sum of his or her ranks in the two rounds. In the overall standings the chefs were ranked by total (a lower total is better) using the same convention: a chef's overall rank is 1 more than the number of chefs with a strictly lower total.

The following is known:

  1. In Round 1, Ishaan and Manav tied with each other, and Jhanvi was the only chef ranked ahead of them.
  2. Manav's rank in Round 2 was 6.
  3. Kabir was ranked ahead of Ishaan in Round 2.
  4. In Round 2, Ishaan tied with exactly one other chef.
  5. Nikita's rank was the same in both rounds.
  6. Ishaan was the only chef with overall rank 1.
  7. In the overall standings there was exactly one three-way tie and exactly one two-way tie, and no other tie.

sets.title: Badminton Knockout
sets.contentHtml:
Eight players, Rhea, Sahil, Tara, Uday, Vikram, Wasim, Yamini and Zoya, took part in a knockout badminton tournament. Each player was given a different seed from 1 to 8 (seed 1 being the strongest). The draw was as follows:

  • Quarterfinals: QF1 seed 1 vs seed 8; QF2 seed 4 vs seed 5; QF3 seed 3 vs seed 6; QF4 seed 2 vs seed 7.
  • Semifinals: SF1 winner of QF1 vs winner of QF2; SF2 winner of QF3 vs winner of QF4.
  • Final: winner of SF1 vs winner of SF2.

A match is called an upset if its winner had a larger seed number than its loser. Every match produced a winner.

Prize money (in ₹ thousand) was 80 for the champion, 40 for the player who lost the final, 20 for each player who lost in a semifinal and 10 for each player who lost in a quarterfinal. In addition, a player received a bonus of ₹5 thousand for each upset that he or she won.

The following is known:

  1. Exactly three of the seven matches were upsets.
  2. Tara won exactly two matches.
  3. Vikram defeated Uday, and that match was an upset.
  4. Sahil won exactly one match, and it was against Wasim.
  5. Zoya defeated Yamini.
  6. Sahil was one of the top four seeds (seeds 1 to 4).
  7. Rhea's seed number was exactly one less than Tara's.

Key deductions. By conditions 4 and 9, Meera (from Pune) is on the floor just above the Acoustics specialist, so Acoustics is on floor 1, 2, 3 or 4. By condition 8, Acoustics and Optics are at least three floors apart, so (Acoustics, Optics) is (1, 4), (1, 5), (2, 5) or (4, 1).

questions.stemHtml: What was Lavanya's rank in Round 1?
questions.solutionHtml:
Key deductions. By condition 1, Jhanvi's Round 1 rank is 1 and Ishaan's and Manav's are 2. By condition 2, all five other chefs are ahead of Manav in Round 2, so no one else has Round 2 rank 6. Let b be Ishaan's Round 2 rank; his total is 2 + b, and by condition 6 every other chef's total exceeds 2 + b.

  • Jhanvi: 1 + (her Round 2 rank) > 2 + b, so her Round 2 rank is at least b + 2. Since it is at most 5, b ≤ 3.
  • Kabir: his Round 2 rank is at most b - 1, so his Round 1 rank is at least 4.
  • Ishaan's Round 2 tie partner X: X's Round 1 rank + b > 2 + b, so X's Round 1 rank exceeds 2. X is not Manav (Round 1 rank 2), not Jhanvi (behind Ishaan in Round 2) and not Kabir (ahead of him). So X is Lavanya or Nikita.
  • Nikita (rank n in both rounds, total 2n): if she were ahead of Ishaan in Round 2, then n ≤ b - 1, so 2 + b < 2n ≤ 2b - 2, giving b > 4, which contradicts b ≤ 3. So Nikita is not ahead of Ishaan in Round 2.

So only Kabir, and Lavanya if she is not X, can be ahead of Ishaan in Round 2. If X were Nikita, then n = b and 2b > 2 + b gives b ≥ 3, so both Kabir and Lavanya would be ahead and b = n = 3. But no one can have rank 3 in Round 1, since two chefs share rank 2 there. Hence X = Lavanya, only Kabir is ahead of Ishaan, and in Round 2 Kabir is 1, Ishaan and Lavanya are 2. Jhanvi and Nikita have Round 2 ranks 4 or 5, and Manav has 6.

Totals: Ishaan 4, Manav 8, Nikita 2n with n = 4 or 5, Jhanvi 5 or 6, Kabir (Round 1 rank) + 1, Lavanya (Round 1 rank) + 2. By condition 7, the five chefs other than Ishaan have exactly two distinct totals.

  • If n = 5: Nikita 10, Manav 8 and Jhanvi (at most 6) give three distinct totals. Impossible. So n = 4, and Nikita's total is 8, equal to Manav's.
  • Jhanvi's total is not 8, and Kabir's total (at most 7) is not 8, so Kabir's total equals Jhanvi's: Kabir's Round 1 rank equals Jhanvi's Round 2 rank.
  • If Lavanya's total were not 8, she would join Jhanvi and Kabir. Her Round 1 rank is at least 4, so her total is at least 6, forcing totals of 6: Jhanvi's Round 2 rank 5, Kabir's and Lavanya's Round 1 ranks 5 and 4. But Nikita and Lavanya would then tie at rank 4 in Round 1, and the next rank would be 6, not 5. Impossible. So Lavanya's total is 8 and her Round 1 rank is 6.

In Round 1 Nikita has rank 4 and Lavanya 6, so Kabir has 4 (tied with Nikita) or 5. Correspondingly, Jhanvi's Round 2 rank is 4 (tied with Nikita) or 5. Both cases satisfy every condition:

questions.stemHtml: A van starts at P, must pass through both S and T (in either order) and must finish at V. Towns and roads may be used more than once. What is the minimum total travel time, in minutes?
questions.solutionHtml:
Use the shortest travel times between the towns involved:

  • P to S: 70 (P-Q-R-S or P-R-S); P to T: 75 (P-Q-T).
  • S to T: 65 (S-U-T).
  • T to V: 45 (T-V); S to V: 60 (S-U-V).

Order P, S, T, V: 70 + 65 + 45 = 180. Order P, T, S, V: 75 + 65 + 60 = 200.

The minimum is 180 minutes, for example along P-R-S-U-T-V.
